Michael Oluwafemi: The top of the draft board could belong to a receiver. Washington’s Oluwafemi brings generational potential, elite deep-ball ability and the athleticism to rise above defenders. Another standout season could make him the rare wideout with a legitimate case to go first overall.
Kareem Carter: There may not be much room to operate when Carter is tracking the play. USC’s linebacker covers ground in a hurry and has the athleticism to stay with elusive offensive players in space. That rare range gives him an early case for a high selection.
DaQuan Battles: Contact is where Battles starts making his case. Ohio State’s powerful back can keep a rushing attack moving by creating yards after defenders reach him, giving an offense an identity on the ground. His early projection puts even a top-five selection in play.
Zaquan Newton: Newton gives Georgia a defensive tackle with the strength to anchor the middle and control space at the point of attack. His presence changes how offenses have to block the interior. Those traits put him among the class’s elite defensive building blocks entering the season.
Quentin Sosa: Sosa controls the point of attack for Ohio State and can close an interior rushing lane before it develops. The strength he uses against the run also creates opportunities to drive blockers back on passing downs. That two-way impact makes him one of the class’s premier interior defenders.
Jaiden Bloodworth: A 6-foot-6 lineman isn’t supposed to get upfield this quickly. Alabama’s Bloodworth brings movement skills and a substantial frame to the offensive line, giving coaches the flexibility to envision him at multiple spots. His versatility makes him a compelling early prospect.
Azizi Akpabio: Receivers have to earn their space against Akpabio. Arizona’s big, physical corner excels pressing at the line and adds tackling ability to the run defense, giving the secondary a presence who can affect the game before and after a throw.
Will Hoggard: When Hoggard gets going, Stanford’s passing game can gather momentum in a hurry. The quarterback has flashed stretches that put his upside on display, making his upcoming season an opportunity to build on those high points and strengthen his early draft case.
Rontay Jenkins: Jenkins arrives at Tennessee with an arm that can make scouts stop and watch. After producing at Georgia Tech, the quarterback gets a new stage for his elite throwing talent, and evaluators will be watching for another step forward this season.
Zion Ellis: Ellis lets the opening develop before showing why defenses have to account for him. Georgia’s back combines patience and vision with the talent to enter top-ten conversations, giving scouts an intriguing runner to follow as the new season unfolds and blocking looks grow more varied.
Cameron Johnston: Johnston brings rare strength to the Oklahoma offensive line without sacrificing his ability to move. The powerful guard can reach defenders in space and create room in the run game, giving the Sooners an interior presence who can influence plays beyond the line.
Kris Wiliams: Wiliams can make the line of scrimmage feel like contested territory. Michigan’s physical interior defender uses power to control the point of attack and finish plays, giving the Wolverines a force in the middle who demands attention on every snap.
Ameer Young: Young gets one more season to make his case as a franchise quarterback. After starting two years at Missouri, the transfer brings solid production and experience to Clemson, where his final college campaign offers a new stage for an early first-round prospect.
Marquavious Keys: Give Keys the football and Oklahoma’s offense can change speed in a hurry. The compact receiver is a gifted athlete and dangerous playmaker in space, giving the Sooners a top receiving threat whose ability to create can stress a defense from anywhere.
Dillon Bethea: Bethea has a habit of finding the ball and arriving with authority. The former four-star Alabama linebacker combines a physical approach with the recruiting pedigree to attract early attention, giving scouts a defender whose instincts and hitting can set the tone.
Trey Dunham: At 6-foot-8, Dunham gives Texas a massive presence on the right side. The tackle has made it difficult for defenders to get past him, putting him on the early radar as a potential franchise lineman with a clear home on the right.
Isai Fields: Fields brings more than raw speed off the edge for Notre Dame. The technical pass rusher can convert speed into power and has produced strong sack numbers, giving offensive tackles several problems to solve as he builds his early first-round case.
Dejon Stokes: A Michigan touch can turn into a long afternoon for a defense when Stokes finds room. The back has produced big gains and highlight plays across two seasons, putting his ability to create explosive yardage at the center of his early projection.
Jake Fulton: Fulton has the frame and arm to keep an offense thinking downfield. The former three-star recruit began his college career at Texas A&M and now gives Oklahoma State a quarterback whose physical tools are drawing early interest from professional evaluators.
Lee McCain: McCain adds another name to Ohio State’s pipeline of first-round defensive backs. The corner combines strong zone coverage with athleticism and professional-level ball skills, giving the Buckeyes a player who can read the field and turn a throw into an opportunity.
Imanif Ali: Ali’s range gives Arizona State options across the secondary. The safety brings a track background and the athletic ability to cover ground from multiple alignments, offering the defense a versatile presence who can work over the top or move around the formation.
Kenyada Akenzua: Akenzua stands out before the ball is snapped. Central Michigan’s 6-foot-7 right tackle pairs rare size with good leverage in the run game, giving scouts a small-school prospect with the physical traits to make an early first-round case on the edge.
Tre Miles: Miles brings the speed of a former five-star receiver recruit to Georgia’s tight end group. His athleticism allows him to stretch a defense and create chunk plays, giving quarterbacks a target who can turn a seam into a significant gain.
Quintrell Hill: Hill gives Ole Miss a defensive lineman who can affect the pocket from more than one spot. Comfortable on the edge or inside, he uses above-average strength to collapse space and offers a front flexibility when it wants to change its look.
Kerderius Anderson: Anderson brings a burst that can make an interior offensive lineman react in a hurry. Florida’s athletic defensive tackle pairs quick closing speed with explosive movement, giving the Gators a disruptive presence whose range stands out when the play moves away from his gap.
Derick Soliz: Washington can present a very different challenge with Soliz across from its top target. The 6-foot-5 receiver combines size, competitiveness and a large catch radius, giving an offense another option who can contest throws and make defenders account for his reach.
Leialoha Kainoaiko: Kainoaiko gives Utah a guard who can make room for the running game from either side. His reliable run blocking and versatility provide a strong early foundation, while the ability to fill in at right tackle adds another way to use his size.
True Adams: Adams gives Houston a corner with athletic ability and the ball skills to make a throw dangerous. His movement and awareness create opportunities to compete at the catch point, putting him on the early first-round radar as a secondary playmaker.
Alijah Campbell: Campbell brings a captain’s presence to the Oregon secondary. The veteran safety has improved throughout his college career and provides the leadership to organize a defense, pairing that experience with tackling ability that projects to remain useful at the next level.
Jay Maxwell: Maxwell gives Stanford a tight end who can create separation with the smoothness of a receiver. His athletic ability and consistent production make him a compelling early prospect, offering a quarterback a target who can work the route and turn opportunities into gains.
Braidy Foster: Foster has made the middle of Oregon’s line a productive place to build from. The center brings experience with the versatility to play across the interior, giving scouts a reliable anchor whose fit at the position stands out on the early board.
Evan Brown: Brown stands out in a Texas defensive line room filled with professional prospects. The edge rusher combines the size and skill to compete up front, giving an offense another player to account for when the Longhorns send pressure after the quarterback.
